newsitem.title: UK: STYLE HOLDINGS PLANS AIM DEBUT, SEEKS EXPANSION.
newsitem.headline: STYLE HOLDINGS PLANS AIM DEBUT, SEEKS EXPANSION.

text.p: Mens' fashion retailer Style Holdings Plc said on Monday it planned to float on the London Stock Exchange's Alternative Investment Market in August and would use the proceeds to increase its number of retail outlets.
Style raised just under three million stg via a private placing, of which 1.14 million stg will be used to redeem preference shares.
The group said the balance will predominantly be used to fund the nationwide expansion of its Envy stores.
The Envy chain, which sells branded mens' casual wear, has 12 stores in major UK cities and the company said it had identified another 20 sites.
Style made pre-tax profits of 1.53 million stg in the year to February 28 1997, up 82 percent on the previous year. Turnover increased by 24 percent on the year before to 27.25 million stg.
Envy contributed to around a third of group turnover with Style's concessions business generating about two thirds.
The concessions business has 124 shop-in-shops based in 118 host outlets, mostly Burton's Top Man stores.
Shore Capital Stockbrokers Limited have been appointed nominated advisers and brokers to Style.
Style's flotation will be the third by a mens' fashion retailer since July, following Ted Baker plc and Blake's Clothing Plc.
Share dealings are expected to start on August 26.
